question: What domains are covered in the corpus?

answer.free_form_answer: No specific domain is covered in the corpus.
evidence: Common Voice BIBREF10 is a crowdsourcing speech recognition corpus with an open CC0 license. Contributors record voice clips by reading from a bank of donated sentences. Each voice clip was validated by at least two other users. Most of the sentences are covered by multiple speakers, with potentially different genders, age groups or accents.

title: CoVoST: A Diverse Multilingual Speech-To-Text Translation Corpus
answer_short: speech recognition, multilingual translation, tourism, Bible readings
answer_rationale: The evidence indicates that the corpus covers multiple domains: Text 4 mentions CoVoST as a multilingual speech-to-text translation corpus covering 11 languages into English, while Text 5 references tourism (via Woldeyohannis’s Amharic-English corpus) and Bible readings (via Boito2019Mass’s multilingual ST corpus). Text 3 and Text 1 emphasize speech recognition and speaker diversity, which are core to the corpus’s design. These domains are explicitly or implicitly supported across multiple documents.
